title: Atmospheric and Ocean Circulation, ENSO and the Water Cycle
seo_title: Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science: Atmospheric and Ocean Circulation Worksheets
standard_code: Earth and Environmental Science Unit 2: Energy for atmospheric and hydrologic processes
standard_text: Uneven heating and global atmospheric circulation (Hadley cells, trade winds, pressure belts); the Coriolis effect; surface and thermohaline ocean currents, including the East Australian and Leeuwin Currents; ENSO, the Indian Ocean Dipole and Australian climate; the water cycle. (Senior Secondary Earth and Environmental Science, Unit 2: Earth processes – energy transfers and transformations)
meta_desc: Free Year 11 Earth and Environmental Science worksheets on atmospheric and ocean circulation: Hadley cells, the Coriolis effect, the East Australian and Leeuwin Currents, El Niño, La Niña, the IOD and the water cycle. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Winds and currents move heat from the tropics to the poles.
key_sub: Southern Hemisphere: lows spin clockwise; highs anticlockwise.
body_html:
How to think about it

The tropics receive more solar energy than the poles, so the atmosphere and oceans carry heat poleward. Air rises at the Equator and sinks near 30° (Hadley cells), giving subtropical deserts such as inland Australia. Earth's rotation deflects moving air and water to the left in the Southern Hemisphere (the Coriolis effect).

Wind-driven currents such as the warm East Australian Current, and the density-driven thermohaline circulation, move heat around the globe. Changes in the Pacific (El Niño and La Niña) and the Indian Ocean (the IOD) strongly affect Australian rainfall.

Example

La Niña: wetter or drier in eastern Australia?

stronger trade winds pile warm water near Australia

more evaporation and rain

Answer: usually wetter

Example

Which way does a cyclone off Queensland spin?

Southern Hemisphere low pressure

Answer: clockwise

Common mistakes

  • Using the Northern Hemisphere rule: in Australia lows spin clockwise.
  • Thinking El Niño means more rain for eastern Australia.
  • Saying ocean currents are driven only by the Moon.

faq.q: Why does El Niño matter to Australian farmers?
faq.a: El Niño often brings below-average rainfall and higher temperatures to eastern Australia, raising the risk of drought and bushfires.
A slow global ocean circulation driven by differences in temperature and salt content: cold, salty water sinks near the poles and spreads along the ocean floor.

items.e: Deep groundwater may stay for thousands of years.

Why does Tasmania get more rain in winter than in summer?
c: the belt of westerly winds and cold fronts moves north in winter
items.e: Pressure belts shift with the seasons.

items.q: Why does the land heat up faster than the sea?
c: water has a higher specific heat capacity and mixes, so the sea warms more slowly
land has a higher specific heat capacity

items.q: Why is the stratosphere warmer at the top than at the bottom?
c: the air is denser at the top
ozone absorbs ultraviolet radiation from the Sun
it is closer to Earth's core
items.e: In the troposphere temperature falls with height.

items.q: What is the subtropical ridge?
c: a belt of high pressure near 30° S that brings dry, settled weather
items.e: Its position decides whether fronts reach southern Australia.

items.q: Why does a forest have a lower albedo than a desert?
c: dark leaves absorb more sunlight than pale sand
items.e: Clearing forests can change local climate.

items.q: What is a cold front?
c: a warm current in the ocean
the boundary where a cold air mass pushes under warmer air, often bringing a wind change and rain
items.e: Cold fronts cross southern Australia from the west.

items.q: What is the Great Artesian Basin?
c: one of the largest underground freshwater reservoirs in the world, under inland eastern Australia
a salt pan in South Australia
a lake in the Snowy Mountains
items.e: Water seeps in at the Great Dividing Range.

items.q: What happens during a La Niña event?
c: trade winds strengthen, warm water builds up near Australia and eastern Australia is often wetter
items.e: The 2010–12 and 2020–22 La Niñas brought major floods.

items.q: Why does upwelling off Peru weaken during El Niño?
c: the fish eat all the nutrients
the trade winds weaken, so less cold, nutrient-rich water is pulled to the surface
items.e: Fisheries collapse during strong El Niños.

items.q: How does the Southern Annular Mode (SAM) affect southern Australia?
c: it changes the speed of the Leeuwin Current only
it shifts the westerly winds north or south, changing winter rainfall
items.e: A positive SAM in winter often means less rain in the south.

items.q: What is evaporation in the water cycle?
c: liquid water changing to water vapour, using energy from the Sun
items.e: Most evaporation is from the oceans.

items.q: Which gases are the main natural greenhouse gases?
c: water vapour, carbon dioxide and methane
items.e: N₂ and O₂ do not absorb infrared.

items.q: What is the Coriolis effect in the Southern Hemisphere?
c: moving air and water are deflected to the left
air moves straight from high to low pressure
moving air is deflected to the right
items.e: In the Northern Hemisphere they are deflected to the right.

items.q: Which way does air circulate around a high-pressure system in the Southern Hemisphere?
Why does the Equator receive more solar energy per square metre than the poles?
c: sunlight hits it more directly, so the energy is spread over a smaller area
it is closer to the Sun
items.e: At the poles the same beam is spread out.

items.q: Why are many of the world's deserts, including much of inland Australia, found near 30° latitude?
c: it is closest to the Sun
dry air sinks there in the descending branch of the Hadley cell
items.e: Sinking air warms and dries out.

items.q: What is the global conveyor belt?
c: the worldwide thermohaline circulation linking all the oceans
items.e: A full circuit may take about 1000 years.

items.q: What is the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD)?
c: a difference in sea surface temperature between the western and eastern Indian Ocean that affects Australian rainfall
items.e: A positive IOD often means less rain in south-eastern Australia.

items.q: Water has a very high heat capacity. Which effect on Earth's surface does this cause?

Rivers carve valleys and build deltas.
Oceans and lakes keep nearby climates milder.
Ice in cracks pries rocks apart (frost wedging).
items.e: Water's unusual properties shape Earth's surface.
